top_8.name: is_solid

structs_touched.via: param 1 (const in effect -- no stores found)

top_8.description: KNOWN. Pure predicate over a Tmap* and a pixel (x,y): computes a room-row index i = 29 - ((y+1)>>4), range-checks it against [0,31] (Tmap.room has 32 Tfloor entries per it_types.h), loads room[i], and returns 0 if the row index is out of range or room[i].empty != 0 or x's column falls outside [room[i].start_tile, room[i].end_tile]; otherwise returns a computed solid-surface Y coordinate derived from room[i]'s collision-flag word (Tmap.offset-relative math, sign-bit special-cased with a small correction). This is the tower floor-cell collision query used by all three collision-resolution variants (handle_player_collision_original/old/combo). No writes to *map at all -- a true predicate, ideal negative-control target (inject a byte fault and confirm *map stays byte-identical while only EAX diverges).

struct_ranges: *map: none written; assert byte-identical as a negative control
comparison_domain.return_value: int: 0 (not solid / out of range) or computed solid-surface Y

top_8.name: jump_player
globals_read: unnamed float literal @0x4d7130 (.rdata, no DWARF symbol -- deceleration/scale factor)
unnamed float literal @0x4d7134 (.rdata, no DWARF symbol -- comparison threshold)
top_8.description: KNOWN structure/offsets, INFERRED gameplay semantics -- the SECOND pick, WITH x87, chosen specifically as the physics/FP-fidelity test. THE game's jump-launch physics. arg2==0 is a normal jump: fails (returns 0) if status (jumping flag) is already set; otherwise sets status=1, doubles the current horizontal speed sx via x87 (fadd st,st), compares its sign, optionally rescales it by the unnamed .rdata literal at 0x4d7130 for the opposite-direction case, clamps the result against max_speed[collision_type] (the DWARF-named global double array), writes the clamped result into sy (vertical launch speed) and max_s (recorded peak horizontal speed, used later for combo scoring), and -- only on the branch that clears a fucompp/fnstsw threshold test against the literal at 0x4d7134 -- sets rotate=1 and angle=0 to kick off the jump-spin animation. arg2!=0 is a forced jump (e.g. bounce): fails if status is already set (mirrors normal path), else sets status=1 and sy = -(arg2*12) converted int->double via fildl/fstpl, no rotate/angle/max_s touch. This is exactly the case win32_pilot.md SS3 flags as HYPOTHESIS risk: sy/max_s are produced by a chain of fadd/fld/fmuls/fucom ops that GCC 4.4.1 -mfpmath=387 keeps at 80-bit extended precision on the real x87 stack -- a `double`-only LIFTED/NATIVE form can legitimately round differently at the last bit, and this function is small enough to isolate that question cleanly.

struct_ranges: *player: status(+0x34,4B), sy(+0x18,8B, x87-fidelity-critical), max_s(+0x20,8B, x87-fidelity-critical), rotate(+0x50,4B), angle(+0x54,4B); recommend the full 184B Tplayer struct digest plus bit-exact dword compare on sy/max_s specifically (not epsilon-compare)
comparison_domain.return_value: int: 0 (jump refused, already jumping) or -1 (jump accepted)

top_8.name: line_intersect
top_8.prototype: int line_intersect(int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int *, int *)
globals_read: unnamed float literal @0x4d6cb4 (.rdata, no DWARF symbol -- rounding-bias constant, used in an fadd before truncation)
top_8.description: KNOWN, fully decoded -- an ALTERNATE x87 pick to jump_player, offered because it stresses a different part of x87 fidelity: explicit FPU control-word manipulation. Classic 2D line-segment intersection by determinant/cross-product (all 8 coordinates are plain ints, converted to x87 doubles via fildl for the math). Computes the parametric determinant, returns 0 (no intersection) on a degenerate/parallel case caught by three fucom/fnstsw checks against 0.0, 1.0 and the two segments' own parametric bounds; on success it explicitly saves the caller's x87 control word (fnstcw), forces round-toward-zero for two fistpl (int) conversions of the intersection point, restores the original control word (fldcw), and writes the two integer coordinates through the caller-supplied int* out params. The explicit control-word save/switch/restore around fistpl is exactly the kind of x87-state-sensitive code most likely to expose a LIFTED-form fidelity gap (a naive lift using `double`+`(int)` cast silently uses whatever rounding mode C gives it, not FE_TOWARDZERO-forced-then-restored). Slightly over the informal 400B ceiling window boundary is not an issue here (302B, in range) but it is the largest/most complex of the eight.

registers: x87 control word must be observed unchanged after return (the function must not leak its temporary round-toward-zero mode)
comparison_domain.return_value: int: 0 (no intersection) or 1 (intersection found); *out_x/*out_y (8B) valid only when return==1
